items.text: Since that is not an attack on them directly but their methods, it may be inflammatory, but it isn't a direct attack. Saying things like "Democrats are crazy" etc, that would be an attack. That statement you listed would not be in violation of the rule.

Out of curiosity, would you include these examples to be working against ICE and trying to prohibit them from doing their duties?

1. [Ice removed from Monterey County Jail](https://www.thecalifornian.com/story/news/2017/12/18/ice-agent-removed/961693001/)
2. [LA Sheriff Vows to remove ICE from County Jails](https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/Alex-Villanueva-Limit-Cooperation-ICE-503111661.html)
3. [Companies that work with ICE could lose contracts.](https://psmag.com/social-justice/companies-that-work-with-ice-could-lose-california-contracts)
4. [California Expands protections to ICE Workplace Raids](https://www.latimes.com/politics/essential/la-pol-ca-essential-politics-updates-california-expands-workplace-1507236616-htmlstory.html)
5. [California Cops are "Frustrated" at the New Sanctuary Laws](https://www.foxnews.com/us/california-cops-frustrated-with-sanctuary-laws-stopping-them-from-working-with-ice-over-twice-deported-criminal)
6. [New California Law makes it harder for ICE to arrest people in Court Houses](https://psmag.com/social-justice/a-new-law-makes-it-harder-for-ice-to-arrest-immigrants-from-courthouses)
7. [Companies in CA could be fined for voluntarily working with ICE](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2018/01/18/California-employers-could-be-prosecuted-for-voluntarily-cooperating-with-ICE/5341516332264/)

&#x200B;

According to the Fox Example (#5) cops cannot work with ICE unless they attain a signed warrant. In the examples above, California has stated that they want local law enforcement to not even cooperate with ICE in almost any capacity. This goes far beyond just "protecting immigrants" at this point. They are trying to make ICE's job hell to do.

&#x200B;

Imagine being an ICE agent. Your job is to find illegal aliens and deport them. However, no one will work with you, so you have to find the illegal aliens yourself and determine if they are here illegally or not. Then, you have to get a warrant to have someone arrested to be deported. Then you have to find the person, usually conducted in a raid because you can't pick them up at a local courthouse or jail should they be detained etc. These laws are designed to make ICE's job nearly impossible to do, imo.

items.title: Judge indicted in Massachusetts for refusing to allow undocumented immigrant to be detained
items.text: Judge indicted in Massachusetts for refusing to allow undocumented immigrant to be detained

Regardless of your thoughts on immigration, this is not how it is done. This judge went full activist and even had the court recorder stop recording at a certain point within the conversation. Apparently they even escorted the illegal alien out the backdoor. Hopefully they throw the book at the said judge and they lose their seat on the bench.

What's wrong with allowing them to arrest people from a courtroom? It's a convenient location and they don't have to put together a squad to do a neighborhood sweep or send multiple agents after a single person. Seems like a better use of manpower imo. The environment is safe for the person bein detained and the agents donig the detainment.

I don't necessarily agree. When cops arrest a perpetrator, they get an arrest warrant and then apprehend the suspect, be it at their job, at home etc. This is no different for an ICE agent detaining a suspect. The judge clearly knew they were there to apprehend the person in question.  It's a controlled situation in which there are guards around and could easily be transferred to custody.

I see no problem with what ICE done here. I do see a problem with the judge aiding the illegal alien to escape ICE.

I imagine there are situations to where ICE can work out deals with people in that situation. Frankly, I believe that illegal aliens should not have safe spaces and ICE should be raiding churches etc as well. If a person is here illegally, they should be detained, given their court date and that's that.

In cases like this, the person in question had 2 prior convictions of illegal entry. At that point, it becomes more than a misdemeanor. There should be no quarter given and, frankly, if a person can be detained at a court house and the proper procedure followed, then it should be done. Churches that offer sanctuary to illegal aliens are, in effect, aiding and abetting an illegal alien which is against the law and the people there should be charged with the proper punishment. Simply put, laws should be enforced, not skirted and danced around as they are now.

The difference is that ICE has federal jurisdiction. They are tasked with enforcing federal immigration law which covers the entirety of the US. There is no extradition necessary here because the entirety of the US is technically their jurisdiction.
